title.value: Pull supplier email data into an inventory sheet

introduction.value: A built email scraping agent extracts relevant data from supplier emails and updates a Google Sheet in real time for a small e-commerce store.

method.value: The poster built a private script for a friend’s small e-commerce store that watched supplier emails, used OpenAI’s o3-mini plus o1-mini to extract and clean the inventory details, saved the output to CSV, and then uploaded it into Google Sheets. The store owner had been entering the data manually; the poster then sold the same setup to other businesses and handled ongoing maintenance.

outcome.value: They say it saved clients hours each week, improved stock management, and brought in more than $2,000 in revenue. Pricing in the thread was $200 to set up and $50 per month, with the poster saying scaling the service was the main problem.

notes.value: The clearest copyable detail is the business model: $200 upfront plus $50 monthly to keep it running and maintain it.

custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The poster built a private script for a friend’s small e-commerce store that watched supplier emails, used OpenAI’s o3-mini plus o1-mini to extract and clean the inventory details, saved the output to CSV, and then uploaded it into Google Sheets. The store owner had been entering the data manually; the poster then sold the same setup to other businesses and handled ongoing maintenance.
How it went
They say it saved clients hours each week, improved stock management, and brought in more than $2,000 in revenue. Pricing in the thread was $200 to set up and $50 per month, with the poster saying scaling the service was the main problem.
Worth knowing

with

Copy prompt
Build a workflow that watches my inbox for emails from suppliers like [supplier names or label]. For each one, extract [SKU, quantity, price, ship date, order number] and add or update a row in my Google Sheet [sheet name]. It's finished when a test email produces a correct row; flag any email it can't parse for me to review instead of guessing.
